vo.text: Homeowner associations collect dues, pay vendors and hold reserve funds, and most of them do it in spreadsheets.
They need real accounting, and they need to never see each other's books.

scenes.title: Casa Harmony
scenes.tagline: A multi-tenant service desk and ERP for HOAs, modelled on Oracle E-Business Suite.

vo.text: Casa Harmony is a service desk and an ERP for homeowner associations, modelled on Oracle E-Business Suite.

scenes.headline: From a resident's complaint to [a paid vendor.]
bullets: Tickets by category, priority and SLA
Work orders raised against a purchase order

vo.text: Residents report problems through the service desk, and every ticket has a priority, an owner and a deadline.
When a ticket needs a contractor, it becomes a purchase order, and the vendor's invoice is matched against it before anyone gets paid.

scenes.headline: Every journal [balances.] Every fund stands alone.
bullets: Oracle-style chart of accounts, 6 to 15 segments
Subledgers post double-entry journals to the GL
Operating and reserve funds each net to zero

vo.text: The chart of accounts follows Oracle's key flexfield model, and subledgers post balanced double-entry journals to the general ledger.
Any accounting line without a fund is rejected, so operating and reserve funds each balance on their own, and the board sees exactly where the money is.

nodes.title: PostgreSQL 16
nodes.sub: GL balances by period and fund

vo.text: Underneath, it's a FastAPI backend on PostgreSQL sixteen, with a Next.js front end that can run on demo data or the live API.
Every tenant table carries a tenant id and a row-level security policy, so isolation is enforced by Postgres itself, not just by application code.
Enterprise accounting, sized for a neighbourhood.
Read the full case study, and see how it was built.
